# Capacity Planning

## Symptoms
- Recurring scheduling failures or SLO burn from resource saturation

## Diagnosis
1. Pull 30d CPU/memory/restart trends from Prometheus.
2. Compare requests/limits vs P95 utilization.

## Remediation
- Recommend HPA/VPA and node pool sizing.
- Schedule changes in low-traffic window with rollback plan.

## Verification
- Headroom restored; no FailedScheduling for capacity.

# ConfigMap Volume Mount Conflict

## Symptoms
- Pod fails mounting ConfigMap subPath or duplicate keys
- Hot-reload not reflected in container

## Diagnosis
- oc describe pod — mount propagation and subPath
- Verify ConfigMap keys exist

## Remediation
- Fix subPath/key references; restart pod after ConfigMap update if not mounted as volume

## Verification
- Pod Running; application reads expected config

## Source
- https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/configmap/

# ContainerCreating (Stuck)

## Symptoms
- Pod long-lived in ContainerCreating

## Diagnosis
1. Events: image pull, CNI attach, volume mount delays.
2. Check network plugin and storage attachment.

## Remediation
- Fix image pull or CNI; resolve volume attach timeout.

## Verification
- Container transitions to Running within expected window.

# CrashLoopBackOff

## Symptoms
- Pod status CrashLoopBackOff, rising restart count

## Diagnosis
1. `oc logs <pod> -n <ns> --previous` and current logs.
2. Classify: config error vs dependency vs probe failure vs missing secret.
3. `oc describe pod` for probe failures and exit codes.

## Remediation
- Fix config/env via git_patch; create missing Secret/ConfigMap.
- Adjust failing readiness/liveness probes.
- Rollout restart once after fix applied.

## Verification
- Readiness probe passing, restart count stable, pod Ready.

# CreateContainerConfigError

## Symptoms
- Pod stuck CreateContainerConfigError

## Diagnosis
1. `oc describe pod` — missing Secret, ConfigMap, or invalid env reference.
2. Verify referenced objects exist in namespace.

## Remediation
- git_patch envFrom/secretKeyRef or create missing Secret.
- OpenShift: ensure ServiceAccount can mount secrets.

## Verification
- Container starts without config errors; pod Ready.

# CronJob Not Scheduling

## Symptoms
- CronJob exists but no recent Jobs created
- suspend: true or invalid schedule

## Diagnosis
- oc get cronjob <name> -o yaml — schedule, suspend, lastScheduleTime
- Check controller-manager logs if cluster-wide

## Remediation
- Fix cron schedule syntax; set suspend: false
- Resolve Forbid/Replace concurrency blocking

## Verification
- New Job created at expected schedule

## Source
- https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/controllers/cron-jobs/

# Disaster Recovery

## Symptoms
- Region/cluster-wide failure; critical apps unavailable

## Diagnosis
1. Declare severity; map blast radius (namespaces, data stores).
2. Confirm backup freshness (etcd, DB, object storage).

## Remediation
- Fail over to secondary cluster/region per DR runbook.
- Restore from verified backups; validate before traffic cutover.

## Verification
- Critical user journeys pass; RPO/RTO documented.

# etcd Backup and Restore

## Symptoms
- Need cluster state recovery or DR validation

## Diagnosis
1. Locate latest verified snapshot per backup policy.

## Remediation
- Restore only on isolated control plane for validation.
- Document RPO/RTO; test quarterly.

## Verification
- Restored cluster passes workload smoke tests.

# Evicted Pod

## Symptoms
- Pod status Evicted, node pressure events

## Diagnosis
1. Node conditions: DiskPressure, MemoryPressure, PIDPressure.
2. Ephemeral storage usage on pod and node.

## Remediation
- Free disk on node or increase ephemeral-storage limits.
- Delete evicted pod objects; rollout restart workload on healthy nodes.

## Verification
- Replacement pods stable on nodes without pressure.

# FailedPostStart Hook

## Symptoms
- Container killed after failed postStart lifecycle hook

## Diagnosis
- oc logs <pod> -c <container>
- oc describe pod — postStart hook command and exit status

## Remediation
- Fix hook script or increase hook timeout
- Remove hook if non-essential; use initContainer instead

## Verification
- Pod Running; hook completes successfully

## Source
- https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/containers/container-lifecycle-hooks/

# FailedScheduling

## Symptoms
- Pod Pending with FailedScheduling event

## Diagnosis
1. `oc describe pod` — read scheduler message (insufficient CPU/memory, taints, affinity).
2. `oc get nodes`, taints, and allocatable resources.
3. Check PodDisruptionBudget and quota limits.

## Remediation
- Lower resource requests or add node capacity.
- Add tolerations for tainted nodes; relax affinity if too strict.
- OpenShift: check SCC and project quota.

## Verification
- Pod scheduled and reaches Running/Ready.

# Graceful Shutdown Timeout

## Symptoms
- Pod killed after terminationGracePeriodSeconds
- SIGKILL after preStop hook timeout

## Diagnosis
- oc describe pod — termination grace and preStop
- Check application shutdown handling in logs

## Remediation
- Implement graceful shutdown; increase terminationGracePeriodSeconds if justified
- Fix preStop hook duration

## Verification
- Rollouts complete without forced SIGKILL in normal conditions

## Source
- https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle/#pod-termination

# HPA Unable To Scale

## Symptoms
- HPA reports FailedGetResourceMetric or scaling limited
- Replicas stuck at min/max

## Diagnosis
- oc describe hpa <name> -n <namespace>
- Verify metrics-server or custom metrics adapter
- Check resource requests on target deployment

## Remediation
- Install/fix metrics-server; add CPU/memory requests to target pods
- Adjust minReplicas/maxReplicas or metric target

## Verification
- HPA shows valid metric and scales under load test

## Source
- https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/run-application/horizontal-pod-autoscale/

# Incident Commander Checklist

## Symptoms
- Active SEV incident; unclear ownership

## Diagnosis
1. Assign IC, comms, ops, scribe roles.

## Remediation
- Set severity; war-room channel; hypothesis tracking.

## Verification
- All-clear only after technical verification complete.

# InitContainerError

## Symptoms
- Init container fails; main containers never start

## Diagnosis
1. `oc logs <pod> -c <init-container>`.
2. Compare init script expectations vs mounted volumes/secrets.

## Remediation
- Fix init container image, command, or dependencies.
- Ensure migrations/secrets available before init runs.

## Verification
- Init completes; main container reaches Running.

# Insufficient CPU (Scheduling)

## Symptoms
- FailedScheduling: insufficient cpu on nodes

## Diagnosis
1. Sum pod requests vs node allocatable CPU.
2. Identify over-requested deployments in namespace.

## Remediation
- Reduce CPU requests or scale cluster/node pool.
- Spread workloads with anti-affinity if hotspot on few nodes.

## Verification
- Pending pods schedule and become Ready.

# Insufficient Memory (Scheduling)

## Symptoms
- FailedScheduling: insufficient memory

## Diagnosis
1. Compare memory requests to allocatable per node.
2. Check for memory-heavy Pending pods blocking batch jobs.

## Remediation
- Right-size requests; add nodes or reduce replica count temporarily.

## Verification
- Workloads schedule; no Pending for resource reasons.

# Job Failed

## Symptoms
- Job status Failed; pods BackoffLimitExceeded

## Diagnosis
- oc describe job <job> -n <namespace>
- oc logs job/<job> or failed pod logs

## Remediation
- Fix application error causing non-zero exit
- Adjust backoffLimit/activeDeadlineSeconds if transient

## Verification
- Job completes with succeeded >= 1

## Source
- https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/controllers/job/

# LimitRange Violation

## Symptoms
- Pod rejected at admission: maximum/minimum resource violation
- Container limits below namespace LimitRange minimum

## Diagnosis
- oc get limitrange -n <namespace> -o yaml
- oc describe pod <pod> — admission error details

## Remediation
- Adjust requests/limits to satisfy LimitRange min/max/default
- git_patch deployment resources

## Verification
- Pod admitted and Running

## Source
- https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/policy/limit-range/

# Liveness Probe Failure

## Symptoms
- Repeated restarts; liveness probe failures in events

## Diagnosis
1. Compare liveness vs readiness settings.
2. Check app health endpoint under load.

## Remediation
- Fix health endpoint or loosen probe timing.
- Do not disable liveness without understanding deadlock cause.

## Verification
- Restart count stable; pod Ready under normal load.

# Node Disk Pressure

## Symptoms
- Node DiskPressure=True; pods evicted
- EmptyDir or logs filling node disk

## Diagnosis
- oc describe node <node> — conditions and allocated ephemeral storage
- Check /var/lib/kubelet or container runtime disk usage

## Remediation
- Prune unused images/containers; expand node disk
- Reduce ephemeral-storage limits or log volume

## Verification
- DiskPressure cleared; new pods schedule on node

## Source
- https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/node-pressure-eviction/

# Safe Node Drain

## Symptoms
- Planned maintenance on a worker node

## Diagnosis
1. Confirm PDB headroom and replica counts.

## Remediation
1. `oc adm cordon <node>` (or kubectl cordon).
2. `oc adm drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data`.
3. Uncordon after maintenance.

## Verification
- Workloads rescheduled; node safe for maintenance.

# Node NotReady

## Symptoms
- Node Ready=False; pods evicted or pending

## Diagnosis
1. `oc describe node` — kubelet, disk, memory, network conditions.
2. Check cloud provider instance status and CNI pods on node.

## Remediation
- Drain and replace unhealthy node; fix kubelet/CNI root cause.
- Reschedule critical workloads to healthy nodes.

## Verification
- Node Ready=True or workload migrated; SLO restored.

# OOMKilled

## Symptoms
- Container exit reason OOMKilled in `kubectl/oc describe pod`
- Exit code 137, restart loop or single crash

## Diagnosis
1. `oc describe pod <pod> -n <ns>` — confirm Last State / Reason.
2. Compare memory limits vs working set (metrics or `oc adm top pod`).
3. Check node memory pressure and sibling pods on the node.

## Remediation
- Increase memory limits/requests in Deployment manifest (git_patch).
- If transient spike, rollout restart after limit bump.
- OpenShift: verify LimitRange/ResourceQuota not blocking patch.

## Verification
- Pod Running, restart count stable, no OOM events in 5m.

## Rollback
- Revert manifest commit if latency/regression detected.

# PodDisruptionBudget Blocked

## Symptoms
- Drain/eviction blocked; PDB prevents voluntary disruption

## Diagnosis
1. `oc get pdb -n <ns>` and compare minAvailable vs current replicas.

## Remediation
- Temporarily adjust PDB during maintenance window.
- Scale deployment to satisfy minAvailable before drain.

## Verification
- Maintenance completes; PDB still protects availability.

# Incident Postmortem Template

## Symptoms
- Incident resolved; need structured retrospective

## Diagnosis
1. Gather timeline, logs, and change records.

## Remediation
- Document summary, root cause, action items with owners.

## Verification
- Postmortem published; preventive actions tracked to closure.

# Pod Preempted

## Symptoms
- Pod terminated due to preemption by higher priority pod
- Unexpected restarts on congested nodes

## Diagnosis
- oc describe pod — preemption events
- Review PriorityClass on workloads

## Remediation
- Assign appropriate priorityClassName to critical apps
- Add capacity to reduce preemption

## Verification
- Critical pods stable under load

## Source
- https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/pod-priority-preemption/

# Readiness Probe Failure

## Symptoms
- Pod Running but not Ready; readiness probe failures in describe

## Diagnosis
1. Inspect probe path, port, initialDelaySeconds, timeout.
2. `oc exec` curl/wget probe endpoint from debug pod if needed.

## Remediation
- Fix application bind address/port or probe path.
- Increase initialDelaySeconds for slow-start apps.

## Verification
- Ready condition True; Service endpoints populated.

# Resource Quota Exceeded

## Symptoms
- Pod stays Pending with forbidden: exceeded quota events
- Create rejected by admission for CPU, memory, pods, or PVC count

## Diagnosis
- oc describe quota -n <namespace>
- oc describe pod <pod> -n <namespace> — read FailedCreate or quota message
- oc get resourcequota -n <namespace> -o yaml

## Remediation
- Reduce resource requests or replica count in manifest
- Raise ResourceQuota limits with change approval
- Delete unused workloads consuming quota

## Verification
- Pod schedules and reaches Running
- quota used <= hard limits

## Source
- https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/policy/resource-quotas/

# RunContainerError

## Symptoms
- Container fails immediately after create; RunContainerError in events

## Diagnosis
1. Check binary path, entrypoint, and volume mounts in manifest.
2. `oc logs` if any output; inspect `oc describe` for mount or permission errors.

## Remediation
- Fix command/args or image architecture mismatch.
- Correct read-only root filesystem or missing binary in image.

## Verification
- Container starts and passes probes.

# SLO Error Budget Burn

## Symptoms
- SLI degradation; burn rate alerts firing

## Diagnosis
1. Identify burning SLI (availability, latency, errors).
2. Compare burn rate to budget window (1h, 6h, 3d).

## Remediation
- Freeze risky deploys if budget exhausted.
- Prioritize fixes restoring SLI; notify stakeholders.

## Verification
- SLI back within target; burn rate normalized.

# StatefulSet Ordered Pod Not Ready

## Symptoms
- StatefulSet stuck — pod-N not Ready so pod-N+1 not created
- Update blocked on partition or ordinals

## Diagnosis
- oc get pods -l app=<sts> — ordinals and Ready column
- oc describe statefulset — currentRevision vs updateRevision

## Remediation
- Fix lowest ordinal pod first (storage, probes, config)
- Use partition rollback if bad rollout

## Verification
- All ordinals Ready; currentRevision matches desired

## Source
- https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/controllers/statefulset/

# Pod Stuck Terminating

## Symptoms
- Pod remains Terminating beyond grace period

## Diagnosis
1. Finalizers on pod; kubelet not reporting.
2. Volume detach stuck on node.

## Remediation
- Remove blocking finalizers after confirming safe.
- Force delete only after node confirmed dead (last resort).

## Verification
- Pod removed; replacement schedules if needed.

# Unschedulable — Node Taints

## Symptoms
- Scheduler message: node(s) had taint that pod didn't tolerate

## Diagnosis
1. `oc describe node` for taints.
2. Review pod tolerations and node selectors.

## Remediation
- Add matching tolerations or remove incorrect nodeSelector.
- Uncordon dedicated nodes if mis-tainted.

## Verification
- Pod schedules on intended node pool.
